xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2710: Feature PRs keep stale failed checks after red main clears — nothing re-triggers them, so they stay out of the merge gate until manually re-run

plan.title: Feature PRs keep stale failed checks after red main clears — nothing re-triggers them, so they stay out of the merge gate until manually re-run
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: When main goes red, every open feature PR inherits the failing check. When main recovers, nothing re-runs those PR checks: the stale fail stays on the statusCheckRollup, the PAN-2712 reconciler faithfully re-observes it and re-latches the failing_checks blocker (src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts:270-295), and readyForMerge stays 0 forever (src/lib/review-status.ts:401-407). Proven on PAN-2683 / PR #2693: all gates passed, held out of the merge gate until a manual `gh run rerun 29414663205 --failed`. That manual command is exactly what needs automating.
narratives.Proposal: Add a level-triggered stale-check re-trigger service to the dashboard server. Each tick it selects review_status rows carrying failing_checks blockers (reusing getMergeBlockerReconcileCandidates), probes main's run history per repo, computes per-workflow red windows with a pure classifier, and re-runs (`gh run rerun <id> --failed`) each failing run on a candidate PR's current head that is completed, attempt === 1, and created inside a *closed* red window of the same workflow. GitHub's attempt counter is the durable once-only guard; red-window membership is the inherited-vs-independently-broken guard; everything re-derives from GitHub so restarts lose nothing. Blocker clearing afterwards is owned by the existing PAN-2712 reconciler cadence.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No failure-signature matching between PR check names and main's failing set (red-window membership is the guard)
- No new durable transition state, DB table, or state-branch record — idempotency is GitHub-derived
- No new UI/dashboard surface for poisoned-PR visibility — structured server logs only
- No re-runs for PRs outside Overdeck management (no review_status failing_checks blocker → not a candidate)
- No changes to PAN-2712 reconciler cadence or blocker semantics; this service never writes review_status
- No webhook (workflow_run) ingestion — polling only, consistent with the reconcile service's webhook-gap rationale
- No retry loop on a failed `gh run rerun` — one attempt, then log and leave the manual fallback

autoDecisions.summary: Level-triggered condition polling instead of durable edge-triggered red→green transition state.
autoDecisions.rationale: The strike asked for a 'durable transition owner'; deriving the condition from GitHub every tick (main run history + attempt counter) is durable across restarts with zero new persistence, and cannot miss a transition that happens while the server is down — an event-based design would.

autoDecisions.summary: Idempotency via GitHub run `attempt === 1` guard rather than a local re-trigger ledger.
autoDecisions.rationale: After `gh run rerun`, attempt >= 2 permanently, so 'once per PR per transition' is enforced by GitHub state that survives any local wipe. Verified live on 2026-07-15 that `gh run list --json attempt` returns the field. A genuinely broken PR gets at most one gratuitous re-run, then is never touched again.

autoDecisions.summary: Inherited-failure guard = per-workflow red-window membership computed from main's run history; signature matching declared a NonGoal.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue offered 'run predates fixing commit and/or signature match'. Red windows make the time predicate precise and per-workflow, and additionally protect PRs that failed while main was green (independently broken) — strictly stronger than the suggested minimum while simpler than signature matching.

autoDecisions.summary: Candidate population = review_status rows with failing_checks blockers, not all open repo PRs.
autoDecisions.rationale: These are the rows the merge gate actually holds back, they already carry prUrl, and PAN-2712's candidate SQL selects them — reusing the read door keeps scope to Overdeck-managed PRs and makes steady-state (no candidates) cost zero GitHub calls.

autoDecisions.summary: Visibility = structured server logs (per-rerun line + per-tick summary), no UI surface.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires re-triggering to never be silent; logs satisfy that. A dashboard surface was listed only as the fallback if automation were absent.
The user-visible symptom is 'PR stuck UNSTABLE after main recovered'; troubleshooting is where an operator looks, and no existing merge-blocker doc page covers this subsystem.

items.title: Pure classifier: compute per-workflow red windows on main and select poisoned PR runs

expected_outputs: stale-check-classifier.test.ts passes with cases for closed window, open window, multiple windows, attempt>=2, run outside any window, run predating history, and workflow mismatch

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/cloister/stale-check-classifier.ts, a pure module with no I/O. Define `interface WorkflowRun { databaseId: number; workflowName: string; createdAt: string; conclusion: string; status: string; attempt: number; headSha?: string }` matching `gh run list --json databaseId,workflowName,createdAt,conclusion,status,attempt,headSha`. Export (1) `computeRedWindows(mainRuns: WorkflowRun[]): Map<string, Array<{ start: string; end: string | null }>>` — group completed runs by workflowName, sort by createdAt ascending; a window opens at the createdAt of a failing completed run (conclusion in FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS, imported from src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts:192) when no window is open, and closes (end) at the createdAt of the next successful completed run of the same workflow; a trailing failing run leaves end === null (main still red). Non-completed runs are ignored. (2) `selectRerunCandidates(prFailingRuns: WorkflowRun[], redWindows: ReturnType<typeof computeRedWindows>): { rerun: WorkflowRun[]; skipped: Array<{ run: WorkflowRun; reason: 'attempt-exceeded' | 'main-still-red' | 'no-red-window-match' | 'not-completed' | 'missing-attempt' }> }` — a run is selected for rerun iff status === 'completed', conclusion in FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS, attempt === 1 (typeof attempt !== 'number' → skipped 'missing-attempt'), and createdAt falls inside a window of the same workflowName with start <= createdAt and end !== null and createdAt < end... note: createdAt inside [start, end) of a CLOSED window selects; inside an OPEN window (end === null) → 'main-still-red'; no containing window → 'no-red-window-match'. Timestamps compare as ISO-8601 strings (same format from gh) — document this in the module header. Write exhaustive unit tests in tests/unit/lib/cloister/stale-check-classifier.test.ts (mirror the directory convention of tests/unit/lib/cloister/in-flight-guard.test.ts). No timers involved — plain synchronous tests.

items.title: Given a main run history of fail(t1) then success(t2) for workflow CI, computeRedWindows returns exactly one CI window { start: t1, end: t2 }; a trailing fail with no later success produces end === null
selectRerunCandidates returns in `rerun` only PR runs that are completed, failing-concluded, attempt === 1, and created inside a closed red window of the same workflowName

A PR run created inside an OPEN window is skipped with reason 'main-still-red'; a run created while main was green for its workflow (or predating available history) is skipped with reason 'no-red-window-match'; attempt >= 2 produces 'attempt-exceeded'; a missing attempt field produces 'missing-attempt'

The classifier produces its results from literal in-memory fixtures alone (no I/O in the module), and returns conclusions-classification driven by FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS imported from src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts rather than a duplicated set
Async gh adapter: list main runs, list PR-head failing runs with attempt, resolve PR head, rerun failed jobs

expected_outputs: stale-check-github.test.ts passes with execFile mocked: JSON parsing, headSha filtering, rerun success returning true, rerun/list errors returning false/[] with a warn log and no throw

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/cloister/stale-check-github.ts wrapping the gh CLI with promisified async execFile (copy the execFilePromise helper pattern and 30s timeouts from src/lib/cloister/ci-failure-feedback.ts:21-35; NEVER execSync — this code is reachable from the dashboard server). Export: (1) `listRecentMainRuns(repo: string): Promise<WorkflowRun[]>` → `gh run list --repo <repo> --branch main --limit 50 --json databaseId,workflowName,createdAt,conclusion,status,attempt,headSha`. (2) `listPrHeadFailingRuns(repo: string, headRef: string, headSha: string): Promise<WorkflowRun[]>` → `gh run list --repo <repo> --branch <headRef> --status failure --json <same fields>` filtered to r.headSha === headSha (mirror listFailingRuns at ci-failure-feedback.ts:85-113, adding attempt). (3) `getPrHead(repo: string, prNumber: number): Promise<{ headRefName: string; headRefOid: string } | null>` → `gh pr view <n> --repo <repo> --json headRefName,headRefOid`. (4) `rerunFailedRun(repo: string, runId: number): Promise<boolean>` → `gh run rerun <runId> --failed --repo <repo>`; resolve true on success, false + console.warn on any error (in-progress run, expired run, API failure) — never throw. Import the WorkflowRun type from stale-check-classifier.ts. All list functions return [] (and getPrHead null) on error with a console.warn, matching the ci-failure-feedback error posture. Unit tests mock node:child_process execFile.

items.title: listRecentMainRuns invokes gh with --branch main --limit 50 and returns parsed WorkflowRun[] including the attempt field; on gh failure it returns [] and emits a console.warn instead of throwing
listPrHeadFailingRuns returns only runs whose headSha equals the PR's current head oid, discarding failing runs from older pushes

rerunFailedRun invokes `gh run rerun <id> --failed` and returns true on exit 0; on non-zero exit it returns false and warns, and the module never calls execSync (grep of the file produces no execSync match)
getPrHead returns { headRefName, headRefOid } parsed from gh pr view JSON and null on error
Stale-check re-trigger service: tick loop selecting failing_checks candidates and re-running poisoned runs once

expected_outputs: stale-check-retrigger-service.test.ts passes under vi.useFakeTimers covering: happy-path rerun + log, no-candidates tick performs zero gh calls, main-still-red no-op, attempt>=2 skip, failed-while-green skip, once-only rerun across consecutive ticks, global 5-rerun cap, throttle windows respected
typecheck and lint complete without errors

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/server/services/stale-check-retrigger-service.ts as a structural mirror of merge-blocker-reconcile-service.ts (module-level ServiceState, POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000 setInterval with .unref(), exported start/stop functions, exported `__tickOnceForTests`). Tick algorithm: (1) `await Effect.runPromise(getMergeBlockerReconcileCandidates())` (src/lib/overdeck/review-status-sync.ts) and keep rows where blockerReasons contains type 'failing_checks' AND prUrl parses via the same regex pattern as parsePrUrl in merge-blocker-reconcile-service.ts:59 (copy the small helper — do not export/import across services). If none remain, return immediately — the tick must make zero gh calls (NFR-2). (2) Group survivors by repo; for each repo, if its main-probe throttle (MAIN_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS = 3 * 60_000, per-repo Map) allows, call listRecentMainRuns and computeRedWindows; cache the windows per repo within ServiceState alongside the probe timestamp so throttled ticks reuse the last probe. (3) For each candidate whose per-issue eval throttle (EVAL_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * 60_000) allows: getPrHead → listPrHeadFailingRuns(repo, headRefName, headRefOid) → selectRerunCandidates(runs, windows). (4) For each selected run, subject to a global MAX_RERUNS_PER_TICK = 5 cap and an in-memory attemptedRunIds Set<number> (skip if present): call rerunFailedRun; on true, add to attemptedRunIds and console.log `[stale-check-retrigger] re-ran run <databaseId> (<workflowName>) for <ISSUEID> PR #<n>: failed at <createdAt> inside main red window <start> → <end>`; on false, still add to attemptedRunIds (H1 — never loop on a failing rerun). (5) Log skipped runs once per databaseId (in-memory loggedSkips Set) as `[stale-check-retrigger] skipping run <id> for <ISSUEID>: <reason>`, and end the tick with a summary `[stale-check-retrigger] <N> candidate PR(s) with failing_checks; <M> re-triggered, <K> skipped` only when N > 0. stopStaleCheckRetriggerService clears the interval and all Maps/Sets. Errors anywhere in the tick are caught and swallowed with a warn — the service must never crash the server. Tests MUST use vi.useFakeTimers()/advanceTimersByTimeAsync (repo rule — never real timers) and mock the classifier's inputs via vi.mock of stale-check-github.ts and review-status-sync.ts.

items.title: Given a candidate with a failing_checks blocker and a PR-head failing run (attempt 1) created inside a closed main red window, one tick invokes rerunFailedRun exactly once for that run and emits the per-rerun log line naming issue, PR number, run id, workflow, and window
A tick with no failing_checks candidates returns without invoking any gh adapter function (zero gh calls verified via mock call counts)

When main is still red for the workflow (open window), or the run has attempt >= 2, or the run failed while main was green, the tick invokes zero reruns and logs the skip reason once per run id across consecutive ticks

Given a run that was already re-triggered (or whose rerun call failed), later ticks produce zero further rerunFailedRun calls for that run id; each tick emits at most 5 reruns and defers the remainder to subsequent ticks

Per-repo main probes occur at most every 3 minutes and per-issue evaluations at most every 10 minutes under fake-timer advancement; an adapter that throws never escapes the tick (the interval keeps firing)
Start/stop the stale-check re-trigger service from dashboard server boot and shutdown

expected_outputs: npm run build produces dist/dashboard/server.js containing the [stale-check-retrigger] service registration (grep of dist output or build success plus source wiring reviewed in diff)

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/server/main.ts, import startStaleCheckRetriggerService/stopStaleCheckRetriggerService and call the start function directly after startMergeBlockerReconcileService() at main.ts:170, with a matching `console.log('[overdeck] StaleCheckRetriggerService started')`. Add the stop call to the same shutdown path that calls stopCostReconcileService() (main.ts:568). No other boot-path changes. NOTE for review/test roles: this touches the dashboard boot path — per the no-live-boot-hotpatch rule, verification must runtime-boot-test the built dist (throwaway instance) rather than trusting typecheck alone; do not restart the live server into this change unverified.

items.title: Dashboard server boot emits '[overdeck] StaleCheckRetriggerService started' after the merge-blocker reconcile service line, observable in a throwaway boot of dist/dashboard/server.js under Node 22
Graceful shutdown invokes stopStaleCheckRetriggerService so the process exits without a lingering interval keeping the event loop alive (interval is also unref'd)

items.title: Document the stale-check re-trigger behavior and manual fallback in troubleshooting

expected_outputs: lint completes without errors; troubleshooting.mdx renders a section titled to match 'stale failed checks' describing the automation, its guards, its log prefix, and the manual gh run rerun fallback

narrative.Action: Add a section to reference/troubleshooting.mdx (match the page's existing heading/style conventions) titled e.g. 'PR stuck with stale failed checks after main recovers'. It must explain: (1) the symptom — PR shows UNSTABLE / failing `test` check and ready_for_merge stays 0 even though review/test/verification passed and main is green; (2) the cause — the check failed while main was red and GitHub never re-runs it; (3) the automation — the dashboard's stale-check re-trigger service re-runs poisoned checks once (attempt 1 only, only runs that failed inside a main red window, never while main is still red), logging under the `[stale-check-retrigger]` prefix; (4) the manual fallback when automation cannot act (run predates history, attempt already >= 2, dashboard down): `gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`, and that the blocker then clears within one reconcile poll (~10 min). Keep it operator-facing: define 'red window' and 'ready_for_merge' inline per the explain-fully rule.

items.title: reference/troubleshooting.mdx contains a new section that names the symptom, the [stale-check-retrigger] log prefix, and the exact manual fallback command `gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`
The section contains inline definitions of 'red window' and the once-only attempt guard so an operator can act without reading source code
